newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds traded quietly but generally higher on Sunday, as share prices continued to take centre stage in the securities market, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.3 pct to 101.01
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.09 pct to 100.63.
Volume was 143 million shekels, which analysts described as at the low end of the average range.

"There generally was demand for (CPI-linked) bonds, but it was selective," said Miri Dagan, a trader at Clal Insurance, adding that there was some supply for short bonds. Yields of bonds with terms of five years or more held at 4.5 percent, she said.
Unlinked bonds rose slightly, without any change in yield.
"All told, unlinked bonds continued on their trend of the last few weeks, which is positive," said Irit Benzour-Gil of Sahar Securities.
Bonds of more than one year are trading at yields of 14.67 percent on average, which she said pointed to a cut of one to 1.5 percentage points in the base rate over the next 12 months.
She said the short-term outlook for interest rates was harder to gauge. The Bank of Israel is due to announce its February monetary programme on January 27.
Makams continued trading at yields of 14 percent where Benzour-Gil said they had been "stuck" since the start of January.

"Dollar bonds were in a mixed trend," said Dagan, noting that the dollar "was stuck for the time being" at its current level. On Friday, the representive rate was fixed at 3.2490 shekels, almost unchanged from Thursday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
